name: Planning Poker
description: This project describes 'Planning Poker' a digital card game designed to help empower agile and scrum development teams to collectively set their sprint goals. Using anonymous pointing, Planning Poker helps to elicit productive conversations across the team to create shared ownership, knowledge, and understanding.
rawDescription: This project describes 'Planning Poker' a digital card game designed to help empower agile and scrum development teams to collectively set their sprint goals. Using anonymous pointing, Planning Poker helps to elicit productive conversations across the team to create shared ownership, knowledge, and understanding.
highLevelGoals: Enable team members to privately and anonymously submit their estimates for user stories to prevent anchoring bias and encourage independent thinking.
Facilitate the disclosure of differing estimates to trigger discussions, allowing the team to share knowledge and reach a consensus on the effort required for sprint goals.
Allow the Scrum Master to control the flow of the estimation session, including revealing estimates, managing rounds, and ensuring all participants have submitted their votes.
Provide the Scrum Master with a clear view of the team's estimation distribution to identify outliers and guide the team towards a shared understanding of the work.
Enable the Product Owner to present user stories and clarify requirements during the estimation process to ensure the team has sufficient context for accurate planning.
Allow the Product Owner to observe the team's estimation process and final agreed-upon values to validate that the sprint goals align with product priorities and business value.
lowLevelGoals: The system accepts a numeric value representing the effort estimate for a specific user story from the authenticated Team Member, storing it without revealing it to other participants.
The system allows the authenticated Team Member to modify their previously submitted estimate for the current user story before the Scrum Master reveals the results.
The system retrieves and displays the list of all submitted estimates for the current user story to the authenticated Team Member, showing only the values and not the identities of the submitters.
The system allows the authenticated Team Member to post a text comment or justification regarding their estimate or the discussion for the current user story.
The system allows the authenticated Scrum Master to trigger the reveal of all submitted estimates for the current user story to all connected Team Members.
The system allows the authenticated Scrum Master to mark the current user story as having reached a consensus, locking the final agreed-upon value and moving the session to the next item.
The system allows the authenticated Scrum Master to initiate a new estimation round for the current user story, resetting the submission status for all Team Members if consensus was not reached.
The system provides the authenticated Scrum Master with a real-time status view indicating which Team Members have submitted their estimates and which have not for the current user story.
The system provides the authenticated Scrum Master with a statistical summary of the submitted estimates, including the minimum, maximum, and median values, to identify outliers.
The system allows the authenticated Product Owner to add or update the description, acceptance criteria, or context notes for the current user story being estimated.
The system allows the authenticated Product Owner to post a clarification or answer to a question raised by the Team during the estimation discussion.
The system provides the authenticated Product Owner with a read-only view of the final agreed-upon estimate and the discussion history for the current user story.
The system allows the authenticated Product Owner to flag a user story for re-estimation or removal from the sprint if the final estimate does not align with product priorities.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are appropriate for a Planning Poker system, as they align with typical roles in agile/scrum teams. However, the description of "Team Member" is incomplete (cut off), which may indicate missing details or potential omissions.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-defined, functional, and aligned with the software description. They cover all key aspects of Planning Poker, including anonymous estimation, consensus building, session management, monitoring, backlog presentation, and prioritization. No contradictions or omissions were found.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and accurately reflect the functional requirements of the Planning Poker system. Each goal corresponds to a specific action an actor can perform, ensuring clarity and completeness. No contradictions or omissions were detected.
